data.title: Netflix Has 2 Growth Engines That Could Drive Its Stock Higher in 2027
data.summary: Netflix (NASDAQ:NFLX) now reaches an audience approaching one billion people. In Q3, operating income rose 37.26% to $4.46B, and operating margin expanded to 34.6% from 28.2%. The stock has gone the other way. Shares are down 38.32% year to date at $57.83. Netflix enters 2027 with two growth drivers: advertising and live events. Here is how they could carry the stock to $100 per share in 2027. Wall Street Already Sees 46% Upside From Here [...] The average analyst price target is $84.55, which implies about 46% upside. Analysts have issued 7 Strong Buy ratings and 26 Buy ratings. For 2027, consensus calls for revenue of $56.6B and EPS of $3.7667. The 2026 estimate is $3.5837. The 2027 figure has declined from $3.8133 90 days ago. Even so, Netflix has beaten EPS estimates in its last two reports, including a 5.72% beat in Q3. Here's What It Takes for Netflix to Reach $100 [...] - Netflix (NFLX) has dropped 38% this year to about $58, yet analysts' targets imply 46% upside, and $100 would mean a 73% rebound. - Advertising and live events anchor 2027 growth, with the ad tier entering 15 new countries and an NFL Christmas doubleheader headlining the live slate. - Netflix bought back $4.8B of stock in Q3, its largest quarter ever, with $22.3B of authorization still remaining.

data.title: Netflix Stock Is Down 37% in 2026, But the Business Is Still Growing. Here's Why I'd Buy It Before the End of November.
data.summary: Third-quarter results did not look like those of a company in trouble. Revenue rose 11.8% to $12.9 billion. Operating income jumped 37.3% to $4.5 billion, and operating margin widened to 34.6% from 28.2% in the year-ago period. Management guided for 2026 revenue of $51.1 billion, up 13%, and an operating margin of 31.5%, versus 29.5% in 2025. That's a combo of double-digit revenue growth and widening margins. [...] Investors sold anyway. The stock fell as much as 6.7% the next morning, and several analysts trimmed their price targets. At first glance, the reasons look fair. Netflix cut its 2026 advertising revenue forecast from roughly $3 billion to about $2.7 billion, citing slower rollout of some new ad products. Ad revenue is still on pace to grow more than 80% this year, per co-CEO Greg Peters. Management conceded, though, that view-hour growth needs to improve and that the U.S. content group can do [...] Management has been voting with the checkbook, so to speak. Netflix bought back 63.9 million shares for $4.8 billion last quarter (a company record, narrowly edging the Q2 buyback budget) at an average of about $75 per stub. The stock now sits around $59, so the timing could have been better. Still, $22.3 billion of buyback authorization remains, against $8.2 billion of cash and about $12.0 billion of expected 2026 free cash flow. Netflix has leaned harder into buybacks as the stock has slid

With apparently no other takers after a foreclosure auction by Goldman Sachs (GS), Netflix (NFLX) swooped in to buy the nearly century-old Radford Studio Center.
